log.text: Stealth Rock up on P1's side
Toxic Spikes up on P1's side

decisions.rationale: Rotom-Wash + Dragapult lead: Rotom threatens Palafin with 2x Thunderbolt (67-131% range), Dragapult outspeeds entire roster and pressures Meowscarada (Draco Meteor 72-140%) and Mimikyu (2x Shadow Ball). Back Incineroar provides Intimidate cycling + Fake Out to break Mimikyu's Disguise and neuter physical threats; Mega Metagross offers Tough Claws Bullet Punch priority for cleaning. This core handles the expected Palafin/Mimikyu/Meowscarada/Glimmora bring with speed control and type coverage.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Leading Rotom-Wash + Dragapult, back Incineroar + Metagross. Opponent expected to bring Palafin, Mimikyu, Meowscarada, and likely Glimmora or Toxapex. Dragapult outspeeds entire opposing roster. Rotom-Wash walls Palafin's Water STAB and threatens OHKO range with Thunderbolt. Incineroar's Intimidate + Fake Out cycle planned to disrupt Mimikyu and Meowscarada. Mega Metagross cleans with Bullet Punch.

decisions.rationale: Lead Palafin and Mimikyu as the designated sweeper pair to apply immediate offensive pressure on Dragapult and Incineroar; Mimikyu's Disguise+Focus Sash guarantees a safe setup or hit. Back Glimmora for Stealth Rock/Spikes hazard attrition and Toxic Debris passive damage, and Meowscarada as the fastest Pokémon (192 Spe) for guaranteed revenge-killing with Protean-boosted STAB moves.
decisions.notebook: Opponent's core threats are Mega Metagross, Dragapult, and Incineroar. Prioritize speed control and hazard pressure. Palafin flips to Hero form for devastating Close Combat/Waterfall. Mimikyu's Swords Dance under Disguise punishes physical switch-ins. Glimmora must land Stealth Rock early; Toxic Debris punishes special attackers. Meowscarada's Protean makes it an unpredictable revenge killer. Save Toxapex and Aegislash defensive pivoting for later games in the series if matchup warrants.

decisions.rationale: Dragapult faces a possible OHKO from Mimikyu Play Rough (71-112%) and heavy chip from Palafin Ice Beam. Protecting Dragapult wastes both of their turns if they double into it. Rotom-Wash Thunderbolt into Palafin deals 67-131%, threatening a KO and forcing Palafin to either take heavy damage or Flip Turn out. This preserves my speed control and Life Orb attacker while pressuring their Water-type.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Leading Rotom-Wash + Dragapult, back Incineroar + Metagross. Opponent brought Palafin, Mimikyu, and two of {Toxapex, Aegislash, Glimmora, Meowscarada}. Dragapult outspeeds entire opposing roster. Rotom-Wash walls Palafin's Water STAB and threatens OHKO range with Thunderbolt. Mimikyu has Disguise + Focus Sash, making it difficult to OHKO; Disguise absorbs first hit without damage. Incineroar's Intimidate + Fake Out cycle planned to disrupt Mimikyu and Meowscarada. Mega Metagross cleans with Bullet Punch.

decisions.rationale: Mimikyu uses Swords Dance safely behind Focus Sash and Disguise, guaranteeing a free setup boost against likely Dragapult aggression. Palafin targets Rotom-Wash with Close Combat for neutral damage, as Close Combat is completely blocked by Dragapult's Ghost typing. This pairing maximizes Mimikyu's threat for Turn 2 while applying immediate pressure on the less-dangerous foe.
decisions.notebook: Opponent core threats: Mega Metagross, Dragapult, Incineroar. Prioritize speed control and hazard pressure. Palafin needs one switch to reach Hero form for devastating Close Combat/Waterfall. Mimikyu's Swords Dance under Disguise punishes physical switch-ins. Glimmora must land Stealth Rock early; Toxic Debris punishes special attackers. Save Toxapex and Aegislash pivots for later games if matchup warrants.

decisions.rationale: Switch Palafin out to Glimmora to set up Stealth Rock immediately, applying hazard pressure that punishes the opponent's expected switches (especially after Mega Metagross and Dragapult). Glimmora's Rock/Poison typing handles Rotom-Wash's Water moves well and resists Dragapult's Ghost attacks; Toxic Debris will punish Rotom-Wash's special moves. Mimikyu passes because it already has +2 Attack under Disguise and is well positioned to threaten a KO on a future turn with Play Rough or Shadow Sneak once hazards are established.
decisions.notebook: Opponent core threats: Mega Metagross, Dragapult, Incineroar. Prioritize speed control and hazard pressure. Save Toxapex and Aegislash pivots for later games if matchup warrants. Glimmora Stealth Rock is critical early-game. Mimikyu's Swords Dance + Disguise punishes physical switch-ins; keep it healthy for a late-game sweep window.

decisions.rationale: Switch Dragapult to Incineroar for Intimidate (Mimikyu +2→+1, Glimmora -1 cured by Lum). Rotom Volt Switches into Glimmora for chip and pivots to Metagross, preserving both leads and setting up Metagross+Incineroar. Metagross resists Play Rough; Incineroar resists Shadow Sneak. Next turn Mega Evolve Metagross, Bullet Punch breaks Disguise, and Incineroar pressures with Flare Blitz or Parting Shot. Dragapult is preserved as a fast cleaner.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Leading Rotom-Wash + Dragapult, back Incineroar + Metagross. Opponent brought Palafin (fainted), Mimikyu, Glimmora, and one of {Toxapex, Aegislash, Meowscarada}. Dragapult outspeeds entire opposing roster. Rotom-Wash walls Palafin's Water STAB and threatens OHKO range with Thunderbolt. Mimikyu has Disguise + Focus Sash, making it difficult to OHKO; Disguise absorbs first hit without damage. Incineroar's Intimidate + Fake Out cycle planned to disrupt Mimikyu and Meowscarada. Mega Metagross cleans with Bullet Punch.

decisions.rationale: Switching to Dragapult risks an instant OHKO from Mimikyu's +1 Play Rough (108–165%). Metagross resists Play Rough (18–27%) and can Mega Evolve for better bulk. Incineroar can Fake Out Glimmora to deny Earth Power, leaving only Mimikyu's attack into a resistant Metagross. Dragapult is preserved as a fast cleaner without SR chip for later.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Leading Rotom-Wash + Dragapult, back Incineroar + Metagross. Opponent brought Palafin (fainted), Mimikyu, Glimmora, and one of {Toxapex, Aegislash, Meowscarada}. Dragapult outspeeds entire opposing roster. Rotom-Wash walls Palafin's Water STAB and threatens OHKO range with Thunderbolt. Mimikyu has Disguise + Focus Sash, making it difficult to OHKO; Disguise absorbs first hit without damage. Incineroar's Intimidate + Fake Out cycle planned to disrupt Mimikyu and Meowscarada. Mega Metagross cleans with Bullet Punch. Metagross is the safer switch-in vs Mimikyu due to Play Rough resistance; Dragapult must avoid Play Rough OHKO.

decisions.rationale: Glimmora sets Stealth Rock to apply critical early-game hazard pressure on all foe switch-ins. Mimikyu uses Play Rough into Dragapult, which is super-effective (2x Fairy) and benefits from the +2 Attack boost while Disguise keeps Mimikyu safe this turn, heavily damaging the series' top threat.
decisions.notebook: Opponent core threats: Mega Metagross, Dragapult, Incineroar. Prioritize speed control and hazard pressure. Stealth Rock is set. Mimikyu Disguise still active. Save Toxapex and Aegislash pivots for later games if matchup warrants.

decisions.rationale: Meteor Mash from Mega Metagross guarantees the KO on Glimmora (78.9-141.8% pre-Tough Claws, even higher with Tough Claws). After Mega Evolving, Metagross hits 162 Speed, always outspeeding Glimmora (116-151), so Glimmora never moves. Incineroar Protects to avoid the likely Play Rough KO from Mimikyu. Metagross takes at most one Shadow Ball from Mimikyu (32.3-58.1%), surviving comfortably from 94%. This removes the hazard setter and preserves both Pokémon for the 2v1 against Mimikyu next turn.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Opponent's remaining roster: Mimikyu (Disguise+Sash intact), Glimmora (58%), and one unrevealed of {Toxapex, Aegislash, Meowscarada}. Mega Metagross at 162 Speed outspeeds entire revealed foe roster except possible speed tie with max-Speed Mimikyu. Incineroar's Fake Out expired after turn 2 switch-in; cannot use it again until switched out and back. Rotom-Wash is immune to Glimmora's Earth Power via Levitate and OHKOs Glimmora with Hydro Pump. Dragapult is OHKO'd by Mimikyu's +1 Play Rough; keep it away from Mimikyu until Disguise is broken.

decisions.rationale: Both active Pokémon target Metagross, the most dangerous remaining threat capable of Mega Evolution. Glimmora's Earth Power is super-effective (2×) and unaffected by its Attack drop since it's special. Mimikyu's Shadow Sneak is super-effective (2×) with priority +1 and boosted by its +1 Attack. Eliminating Metagross before it can Mega Evolve or fire off high-damage moves is the highest-value play.
Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Metagross Protects to blank the likely Dark Pulse from Meowscarada, which otherwise has a chance to OHKO (52.9–85.2% into 55%). Incineroar uses Parting Shot on Meowscarada; Meowscarada always outspeeds Incineroar, so Brick Break could KO first (40.6–59.4% into 43%), but if the opponent targets Metagross with Dark Pulse or if Brick Break rolls low, Parting Shot connects, dropping Meowscarada's Atk/SpA by 1 and pivoting to Rotom-Wash. Rotom-Wash takes only Stealth Rock (12.5%) thanks to Levitate avoiding Toxic Spikes. Even if Incineroar is KO'd, Metagross is preserved and Rotom-Wash enters safely.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Opponent's remaining: Mimikyu (Disguise+Sash intact, +1 Atk), Meowscarada (Protean, Expert Belt, Naive). My bench: Dragapult (100%, Life Orb, Timid), Rotom-Wash (54%, Sitrus, Timid). Metagross-Mega at 162 Speed; Meowscarada 157–192, Mimikyu 127–162. Dragapult is OHKO'd by +1 Play Rough and takes 70.6–110.4% from Dark Pulse—keep it away until Disguise is broken and Mimikyu is manageable. Rotom-Wash is a safe pivot: immune to Toxic Spikes, resists Dark, and threatens both foes with Thunderbolt/Hydro Pump. Break Disguise with Bullet Punch before committing strong attacks into Mimikyu.

decisions.rationale: Incineroar's Parting Shot forces a switch. Rotom-Wash is the clear choice: immune to Toxic Spikes via Levitate, resists Meowscarada's Dark Pulse (12–31%), and survives +1 Play Rough (34–82%) with Sitrus Berry recovery. Dragapult is OHKO'd by +1 Play Rough and takes 49–72% from Dark Pulse — far too risky. Metagross-Mega stays in to break Mimikyu's Disguise with Bullet Punch next turn; it survives one +1 Shadow Sneak (31–47%) from 55% HP.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Opponent's remaining: Mimikyu (Disguise+Sash intact, +1 Atk), Meowscarada (Protean, Expert Belt, Naive, currently Dark-type). My bench: Dragapult (100%, Life Orb, Timid), Rotom-Wash (54%, Sitrus, Timid). Metagross-Mega at 162 Speed; Meowscarada 157–192, Mimikyu 127–162. Dragapult is OHKO'd by +1 Play Rough and takes 70.6–110.4% from Dark Pulse — keep it away until Disguise is broken and Mimikyu is manageable. Rotom-Wash is a safe pivot: immune to Toxic Spikes, resists Dark, and threatens both foes with Thunderbolt/Hydro Pump. Break Disguise with Bullet Punch before committing strong attacks into Mimikyu.

decisions.rationale: Both Pokémon focus-fire on Metagross-Mega, the biggest remaining threat at 55% HP. Mimikyu's Shadow Sneak (priority +1, Ghost STAB 2x vs Steel/Psychic) strikes first; Metagross-Mega's only faster response is Bullet Punch (also priority +1), but Mimikyu's intact Disguise absorbs it for zero damage. Meowscarada's Dark Pulse (special, 2x vs Psychic) follows at priority 0, giving Metagross-Mega two super-effective hits in one turn and a high probability of KO. Incineroar at 43% is manageable next turn after the primary threat is removed.

Bullet Punch breaks Mimikyu's Disguise at +1 priority regardless of speed ties with Shadow Sneak. Rotom Protect (+4) shields it from Energy Ball and Play Rough, both of which can OHKO or nearly OHKO Rotom. If both foes target Metagross, Dark Pulse + Shadow Sneak deals 68.4–103.9% — Metagross may fall, but that lets Incineroar enter freely with Intimidate. If they split or target Rotom, Metagross survives and Disguise is still broken. Either way we remove Disguise and preserve Rotom, setting up a strong next turn.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Disguise must be broken before committing strong attacks into Mimikyu. Rotom-Wash is the safest pivot — immune to Toxic Spikes, resists Dark, threatens both foes. Dragapult is OHKO'd by +1 Play Rough and takes 70.6–110.4% from Dark Pulse; keep it benched until Disguise is gone and Mimikyu is manageable. Incineroar's Intimidate is valuable for neutralizing Mimikyu's Attack boosts.

decisions.rationale: Meowscarada's Dark Pulse is 2x super-effective against Metagross-Mega (24.6–46.5% damage) and makes Meowscarada Dark-typed via Protean, immunizing it to Metagross-Mega's Zen Headbutt. Mimikyu's Play Rough targets Rotom-Wash for a possible KO (43.9–81.6% damage vs 67% HP, ~61% KO probability with +1 Atk). Spreading damage across both active foes maximizes immediate pressure and expected value rather than stacking on Metagross-Mega where neither hit alone can KO and the combined KO is not guaranteed.

Metagross at 17% dies to any attack; switching it to Incineroar triggers Intimidate (Meowscarada → -2 Atk, Mimikyu → 0 Atk), absorbs Stealth Rock + Toxic Spikes poison which Lum Berry immediately cures. Rotom switches to Dragapult, taking only Stealth Rock. Both switches resolve before moves, so the opponent's likely Shadow Sneak → Metagross slot hits Incineroar for negligible damage (Dark resists Ghost) and Flower Trick → Rotom slot hits Dragapult for minimal damage (Dragon resists Grass, -2 Atk). This preserves both weakened Pokémon, neutralises Mimikyu's Attack boost, and brings Dragapult safely onto the field.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Disguise is broken. Mimikyu's +1 Play Rough OHKOs Dragapult; even at 0 Atk it can OHKO with a high roll. Incineroar's Intimidate is essential for neutralising Mimikyu. Lum Berry absorbs one Toxic Spikes layer on switch-in. Metagross at low HP should be preserved for a final Bullet Punch. Rotom is the safest pivot — immune to Toxic Spikes, resists Dark.

decisions.rationale: Mimikyu-Busted Shadow Sneak (priority +1, Ghost super-effective vs Psychic) guarantees KO on 16% Metagross-Mega before it can act. Meowscarada Flower Trick (Grass Physical, super-effective vs Water) targets Rotom-Wash at 67% HP for a possible KO (estimated 41-81% damage). This dual-target strategy can eliminate both active foes in one turn, dramatically shifting the 2v4 board state. Even if Protect blocks one hit, at minimum the faster Shadow Sneak removes the biggest remaining threat.
decisions.notebook: Opponent core: Mega Metagross, Dragapult, Incineroar. Stealth Rock + Toxic Spikes on their side. Mimikyu Disguise already broken. Prioritize speed control and hazard pressure. Save pivots for later games if needed.

decisions.rationale: Incineroar cannot Fake Out (not first turn out). Protect forces Mimikyu's Shadow Sneak onto Dragapult; Dragapult survives the 33–51% roll more often than not, then outspeeds Meowscarada and fires Shadow Ball into Mimikyu for 72–132% — a strong chance to KO the Sash-broken Mimikyu before Meowscarada's Dark Pulse lands. This maximises Dragapult's impact before it falls.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Disguise is broken. Mimikyu's +1 Play Rough OHKOs Dragapult; even at 0 Atk it can OHKO with a high roll. Incineroar's Intimidate is essential for neutralising Mimikyu. Lum Berry absorbs one Toxic Spikes layer on switch-in. Metagross at low HP should be preserved for a final Bullet Punch. Rotom is the safest pivot — immune to Toxic Spikes, resists Dark. Fake Out requires first turn out; Incineroar entered turn 6 so cannot Fake Out turn 7.

decisions.rationale: Bullet Punch (priority +1) always goes first, dealing 28.4–55.6%. If Meowscarada targets Metagross with any move, Incineroar survives and Flare Blitz adds 83.1–160.3%; the combined minimum 111.5% guarantees the KO and wins the game. Only Brick Break onto Incineroar prevents Flare Blitz, but that line loses for us regardless of which teammate we send. Sending Metagross punishes every other opponent move choice and gives a slim chance (two high-roll Bullet Punches) even if they Brick Break Incineroar. Forfeiting is premature while a win condition exists.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Bullet Punch + Flare Blitz combined minimum 111.5% into Meowscarada guarantees a KO if Incineroar survives to move. Opponent's only counterplay is Brick Break onto Incineroar before Flare Blitz resolves.

decisions.rationale: Play Rough guarantees KO on Dragapult (59.5-111.7% damage on 51% HP target across all legal IVs/EVs). Dark Pulse adds 30.8-57.7% super-effective damage to the same target. Even if Dragapult uses Protect (priority +4 goes first), both moves are blocked but we lose nothing—Protect PP is limited and Incineroar at 5% cannot threaten our position. If Dragapult doesn't Protect, Dragapult is KO'd and we have a winning 2v1 against the 5% Incineroar.
decisions.notebook: Opponent core: Mega Metagross (16%), Dragapult, Incineroar. Stealth Rock + Toxic Spikes on foe side. Mimikyu Disguise broken. Save pivots (Rotom-Wash, remaining teammates) for later games. Prioritize speed control and hazard pressure in future games.

decisions.rationale: Bullet Punch always goes first due to +1 priority. If opponent targets Metagross with Dark Pulse, Incineroar survives and Flare Blitz lands; combined minimum 111.5% guarantees KO. If opponent Brick Breaks Incineroar, Incineroar faints before moving and we lose, but this is our only win condition — switching Incineroar to Rotom sacrifices Flare Blitz and leaves us unable to OHKO Meowscarada across multiple turns. We must hope opponent chooses Dark Pulse on Metagross over the safer Brick Break on Incineroar.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Bullet Punch + Flare Blitz combined minimum 111.5% into Meowscarada guarantees KO if Incineroar survives to move. Opponent's Brick Break onto Incineroar is the counterplay that beats this. Incineroar cannot switch back in due to Stealth Rock (25% chip on Fire-type at 5% HP).

decisions.rationale: Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Brick Break into Incineroar guarantees a KO (5% HP, 2x super-effective, STAB via Protean, even at -2 Atk). After removing Incineroar and its Fake Out priority threat, Meowscarada outspeeds Metagross-Mega (192 vs 130-162) and Dark Pulse cleanly KO's it at 10% HP (guaranteed 24.6-46.5% damage). Mimikyu-Busted is already fainted, so the only legal action is Pass.

Bullet Punch has +1 priority and always goes first, dealing 28.4–55.6% to 49% HP Meowscarada with a chance to OHKO. Thunderbolt adds 20.2–38.4%; combined minimum 48.6% leaves Meowscarada at 0.4% only on double-minimum rolls. In that edge case, Meowscarada KOs one ally next turn but the other finishes it. Any other roll combination KOs outright. Opponent's best response (Dark Pulse into Metagross) is irrelevant if Bullet Punch KOs, and if it doesn't, Thunderbolt cleans up after Metagross falls. Thunderbolt's 100% accuracy avoids Hydro Pump's miss risk.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Opponent down to last Pokémon Meowscarada. Bullet Punch + Thunderbolt secures the win barring extreme low rolls. If game continues, Rotom-Wash and Metagross-Mega can clean up.

decisions.rationale: Dark Pulse into Metagross-Mega secures the KO on the 10%-HP Steel/Psychic target with super-effective damage and Protean STAB. This leaves a favorable 1v1 against Rotom-Wash, whose moves are resisted 0.5x by Meowscarada while my Grass coverage (Energy Ball/Flower Trick) is super-effective with STAB. Mimikyu is fainted and can only pass.
decisions.notebook: Opponent core: Mega Metagross, Dragapult, Incineroar. Stealth Rock + Toxic Spikes on foe side. Mimikyu Disguise broken. Save pivots (Rotom-Wash, remaining teammates) for later games. Prioritize speed control and hazard pressure in future games.

reflections.summary: Early KO on Palafin with Rotom-Wash's Thunderbolt gave a 4-3 lead. Effective use of Protect and pivoting maintained momentum, while Stealth Rock and Toxic Spikes chipped the opponent. Priority Bullet Punch and Shadow Ball cleaned up weakened threats, and Rotom-Wash finished Meowscarada after Metagross brought it to 1%.
reflections.adjustment: Opponent may bring Toxapex or Aegislash next game. Consider a check like a Ground-type or strong special attacker that bypasses King's Shield. Be cautious of hazard stacking; limit switches or bring hazard removal. Preserve Incineroar for Intimidate cycling against physical attackers like Mimikyu and Meowscarada.
reflections.notebook: Opponent tendencies: Leads with Palafin + Mimikyu, uses Swords Dance early. Glimmora sets Stealth Rock and has Lum Berry; Toxic Debris sets Toxic Spikes on KO. Meowscarada is mixed (Dark Pulse, Brick Break, Flower Trick, Energy Ball) with Expert Belt and Protean, often becomes Dark-type. Mimikyu carries Shadow Ball (special) alongside physical moves. Toxapex and Aegislash not brought Game 1, likely to appear Game 2. Future plan: Prepare for Toxapex (Regenerator, Haze, Toxic) and Aegislash (King's Shield, mixed attacks). Bring Taunt or strong special attackers. Keep Rotom-Wash healthy for Meowscarada. Break Mimikyu's Disguise with multi-hit or priority before it sets up.

reflections.summary: Lost primarily because the opponent's Mega Metagross with priority Bullet Punch overwhelmed my team after Mimikyu's Disguise broke. Dual hazards (Stealth Rock + Toxic Spikes) chipped down my squad, and I had no Mega Evolution to contest the opponent's Mega Metagross. Palafin was a poor lead (took super-effective Thunderbolt and died immediately), and after Glimmora fulfilled its hazard-setting role and Mimikyu lost Disguise, Meowscarada alone could not overcome the combined pressure of priority, hazards, and Rotom-Wash's Thunderbolt.
reflections.adjustment: Bring a Mega Stone holder in the next game to contest the opponent's Mega Metagross. Protect Mimikyu's Disguise by leading with a safer pivot instead of Palafin, and ensure a faster priority user or speed control option is available to handle Bullet Punch.
reflections.notebook: Opponent core: Mega Metagross (Adamant, Bullet Punch priority), Dragapult (Timid, special attacker), Incineroar (Intimidate support, Parting Shot pivot). Opponent runs dual hazards (Stealth Rock + Toxic Spikes via Glimmora's Toxic Debris). Opponent uses Lum Berry and Sitrus Berry for sustain. Intimidate + Parting Shot strategy weakens and pivots safely. Dragapult carries Thunderbolt for Water-type coverage. Opponent likely has Mega Metagross as a centerpiece—must bring own Mega Evolution next game. Mimikyu Disguise is single-use; do not waste it on non-threatening targets. Prioritize speed control and a safer lead in Game 2.
